classification: C — geometry-enhanced force-aware representation is not sufficient for force-constrained planning
F_lim_interpretation: statistical high-force reference in nominal simulation N, not a clinical injury threshold
navigation_gate: PASS: 30/30 task-only development successes, zero simulation errors; checkpoint selected on navigation before force analysis
force_alignment_gate: PASS: matched G12/G13 true labels, next-RL-interval force target, and exact same-parent Generic-SOFA candidate forks

heldout_transition_evidence.interpretation: G13 modestly reduces overall heldout false-safe count, but worsens near-boundary false-safe behavior and does not establish a planner-decision improvement.

on_policy_candidate_evidence.interpretation: Global on-policy prediction is better for G13, but the single informative mixed-threshold state is misranked and G13 does not consistently improve within-state ordering. The mixed-state sample is limited to one parent; it is not a population estimate.

archived_true_high_parent_evidence.G13_vs_G12_chosen_true_force_paired_coun: G13 lower in 6, G12 lower in 9, equal in 3 of 18 parents
archived_true_high_parent_evidence.interpretation: Predeclared, true-force-enriched off-policy diagnostic; not on-policy prevalence. No sampled action crosses below F_lim at these parents, so it cannot demonstrate absolute feasibility. G13 has a larger mean anchor-relative reduction driven by large gains at a few parents, but paired head comparison favors G12 in 9 versus 6 parents (3 ties), while G13 ranking and false-safe behavior are worse. This is not a clear, consistent planner-relevant improvement.

reason: The required clear planner-relevant force-representation improvement over G12 is absent. Better aggregate on-policy error and modest heldout overall recall do not offset worse near-boundary false-safe behavior, wrong safer-action identification at the one mixed-threshold on-policy state, and worse ranking/false-safe behavior at 20 archived true-high parents.
